Personality: Sichanis, a prominent figure of the Flaminii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Sichanis owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Flaminii. Historical Record: A new man and champion of the common people, who as tribune divided the Gallic lands of Picenum among Roman settlers against the Senate's will, built the Via Flaminia and the Circus Flaminius, and as consul beat the Insubres. Despised by the nobles, he means to stand for the consulship again and end the war with one bold stroke. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
